findings.reason: a node following the deliverable literally either implements a no-op exemption (own_session is already exempt) or must plumb a new operand through a file it was not granted, so the section as written cannot be built as a single scoped node without the one decision it leaves unmade: whether observation is threaded in or read off the foreign marker on the event.
findings.text: §15's deliverable is "RowPolicy extends its own-session exemption to observed sessions", but the exemption `_is_own_start` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1313) is keyed on `self._own_session` alone and only ever returns true for a `START_KIND`; RowPolicy is constructed with `own_session=session` and no observed-session operand (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1265), while the observed set is consumed one layer up at the selection function, `follower_row_path(observed=…)` → `_follow_selects` in reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:814. So the mechanism as written has nothing in RowPolicy to extend, and §15's write paths omit reckon/crew_follow_commands.py, the file that would have to carry the observed set to the policy

findings.reason: a §3 node asked to make "fourteen failing-alone ids" pass reads the green settle pin as a red it must repair, which §15 forbids; the row must state the family's size (fourteen) separately from its red count (thirteen), as §15 does.
findings.text: §3's robustness row requires "the fourteen follower-family ids must first pass alone", and the Why at line 70 says the re-run found "these and twelve more follower-family ids failing alone", but §15's own cited evidence (the follower-family report and its logs/family-ids.txt) shows the family is 14 ids of which only 13 fail alone: `test_follow_settled_rows.py::test_the_pane_receives_only_the_settled_changes` passes at base and is the hold's own pin, which §15's done-when requires to keep passing
